items.quote: Modern Warfare 4 is a confident cinematic shooter that brings almost a decade of storytelling to a satisfying conclusion. Its spectacular set pieces, strong performances, and surprising moral complexity make for a campaign that's hard to put down. With solid multiplayer and the new DMZ mode's tight extraction loop, this is a real return to form.

Modern Warfare 4 is the quintessential Call of Duty experience — both beautiful and violent, endearing and heartbreaking. From a gut-wrenching campaign that is nothing short of a cinematic masterpiece to a thrilling DMZ mode that challenges players' fortitude and a well-rounded multiplayer with new features that keep things fresh, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 might just be the best CoD ever.

It features fluid movement, solid gunplay, a diverse arsenal, and excellent game modes. Furthermore, *Hajin* is, by far, the crown jewel—precisely what the series’ extraction-shooter component needed. As for the campaign, it is fantastic on many levels: it is more intense, dramatic, and emotional, featuring truly memorable moments. This is supposedly the end of the Modern Warfare era, and it certainly concludes on a high note.

Modern Warfare 4 delivers on all fronts, pairing an exhilarating story campaign with tightly balanced, innovative multiplayer and an expansive DMZ extraction shooter mode. Wonderfully presented, it masterfully blends realism with artistic flair and brings meaty and satisfying weapon simulation that elevates every firefight. This is quite simply Call of Duty at its very best.
If you're looking for a rollicking campaign that happens to come with a beefy extraction shooter, you can't go far wrong here.

Modern Warfare 4 is an excellent Call of Duty title and a virtually flawless culmination of the Modern Warfare reboot! The single-player campaign is spectacular and does the franchise proud. The multiplayer is a genuine success, featuring great maps, gameplay that feels both realistic and instinctive, and several pleasant surprises in terms of game modes. Then there’s DMZ, which lays a solid foundation but still lacks the tension and balancing required to be truly convincing. While not absolutely perfect in every single regard, Infinity Ward has delivered an exceptionally solid, polished, and comprehensive entry—one of the best Call of Duty games of this generation.

While the campaign of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 isn’t storytelling perfection, it gives fans a long-awaited taste of that classic Call of Duty experience. Furthermore, learning from the previous installment's mistakes, the DMZ mode has improved by leaps and bounds. On the downside, the direction of the multiplayer mode at launch feels puzzling and raises some eyebrows.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is an exceptional finale to an uneven series. Its return to brutal, linear action and resolute storytelling makes it one of the best Call of Duty games since the original Black Ops.

With a total package of three distinct and fleshed-out modes, Modern Warfare 4 is Call of Duty's strongest argument for a full-length development cycle. When given time and resources, Infinity Ward has shown it can still be at the top of the craft, and that CoD is still a game worth playing each year.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a reminder that sometimes the best way forward is to look back. Rather than chasing trends, gimmicks or trying to reinvent the franchise, Infinity Ward has focused on what Call of Duty does best. That is delivering a memorable cinematic single-player campaign, polished multiplayer, and an ambitious extraction mode with the potential to keep players hooked for months. Each mode has its own strengths, and together they make for a remarkably complete package…Of course, it isn't perfect. The campaign has a few shortcomings, while DMZ needs some refinement. The slower pace of multiplayer might also take some getting used to for those coming from Black Ops 7. But these are relatively minor blemishes on an otherwise outstanding experience. Modern Warfare 4 leans into its strengths without feeling the need to do something outrageous. It's a graphical powerhouse, content-packed, and enjoyable return to form. Call of Duty might not always get the critical recognition it deserves, but with Modern Warfare 4, Infinity Ward has delivered an experience that's easy to recommend.
